content: The tide will turn, however long and bleak the ebb may seem.
author: Celtic & Norse Proverbs
sourceWork: Taghaidh gach uair a h-aimsir — Scottish Gaelic & Maritime Adage
explanation: When the Atlantic tide goes out, it leaves behind muddy flats, exposed seaweed, and stranded boats; it looks as though the ocean has abandoned the shore forever. But the law of the sea is absolute: the water always returns with thunderous renewal. Do not despair during the low ebb.
practicalInsight: If your creative energy, finances, or morale feel at a low ebb today, stand firm. The tide is already turning.
reflectionPrompt: Where in your life are you mistaking a temporary low tide for permanent ruin?
